_provenance.scope: Proposed ten-sol story, new choices, special endings, and balance assumptions; existing six-sol mechanical data remain separately attributed in src/game/scenes.js.

title: Compass Outpost: Ten Sols of Questions

checkpoint.timing: After surviving the decision and finishing feedback, before the shared transition. Compute low-power mode from Energy immediately after the decision, before this supply release or recharge.
checkpoint.explanation: A scheduled reserve compartment already inside the outpost releases sealed oxygen supplies and a charged battery pack. This is not a delivery from Earth or an emergency revival.

feedback.text: The scheduled compartment opens. The crew connects the stored oxygen supply and charged battery pack. DUTİ checks each new reserve reading.
That completes our first chapter. And that little chime? It has returned. Three notes, a pause, then three notes again. Tomorrow, let us find out what is making it.

story.text: Red hills fill the window of Compass Outpost. Two astronauts wave from the airlock. Beside them, a small robot holds a badge almost as wide as its face.
Welcome, Commander! I am DUTİ. Ten sols, one outpost, and a whole notebook of questions. Our first research review is on Sol 6. After that, we prepare our discoveries for the next crew.
DUTİ draws an empty dot in its notebook. Outside, dusty panels need attention. Inside, the storm shelter still needs supplies.
What should we prepare first? Small choices can leave very long trails.
A battery light blinks. Beyond the window, a striped rock catches the morning light. DUTİ turns off one screen to keep the important systems running.
We cannot power every job at once. We can make oxygen, collect that rock, or study the measurements we already have indoors.
The rock is interesting, but the oxygen tank matters too. DUTİ leaves a blank space in the notebook: What could we learn if we saved something for later?
A leaf taps the greenhouse window. These plants were growing before your team arrived. One tray is almost ready to harvest; another still has much to do.
The lights use energy. We can care for all the experiment plants, keep a smaller group, or switch the greenhouse off and use our packaged food.
On a shelf sits an empty seed box labeled NEXT CREW. Nothing goes inside it yet.
A future is a little like a garden. Somebody has to begin looking after it before it arrives.
An Earth message window opens beside the rover controls. DUTİ has found two possible settings, but does not know which uses less energy.
For our fictional mission today, a signal takes about twenty minutes each way. We can ask Earth and wait, use our checklist, or refill oxygen while we have the chance.
Beside the message window, an old equipment list shows a tiny lantern symbol. DUTİ saves the page without knowing why it feels familiar.
A reply can help us think. It cannot skip the journey between the planets.
The outdoor-work light changes to a warning symbol. DUTİ opens the shelter map. The crew can stay inside while the robot takes measurements, or pause research and move into the shelter.
Our sensors warn of increased solar-particle risk. Protecting people comes first. An astronaut could try to finish outside, but that would use oxygen and greatly reduce our safety margin.
A faint three-note chime appears in a saved equipment log. There is no urgent message attached. DUTİ marks it: investigate later, when the crew is safe.
Local sensors show that the fictional solar event has subsided. DUTİ places three research cards on the desk: laboratory, exploration route, and greenhouse.
First research review! The rock you saved, the plants you cared for, and the supplies you kept have changed what we can do. We have time for one study today.
A sealed reserve compartment is scheduled to open after the review. Its oxygen supplies and charged battery pack were stored here before your arrival.
Which study shall we complete? Then we can prepare our discoveries for the next crew. There are still four sols of questions ahead.

transition.note: Scheduled reserve release, then the usual shared transition. This is a checkpoint, not the final ending.

choiceTextOverrides.futureConsequence: The Sol 6 laboratory study will award 4 Science instead of 2.

feedback.text: The sample is here! We recorded observations outside. At the Sol 6 research review, we can study the rock more closely in the lab. We used some of our suit oxygen.

choiceTextOverrides.futureConsequence: Prepare a harvest and detailed growth records. The Sol 6 greenhouse study will award 3 Science.

feedback.text: The plants have the light and care they need. We can study the harvest at the Sol 6 research review. We used more energy today to prepare for that.

choiceTextOverrides.futureConsequence: Prepare a smaller harvest and fewer records. The Sol 6 greenhouse study will award 2 Science.
Lose the harvest study. The Sol 6 report from existing records will award only 1 Science.
Gain extra observations, but lose enough safety margin to close the Sol 6 crewed outdoor task.
choiceTextOverrides.warning: High risk: Safety −4. The Sol 6 outdoor task will become unavailable.

feedback.text: We recorded extra measurements, but exposed our crew to more risk. We no longer have enough safety margin for another crewed outdoor task on Sol 6.

scenes.title: The Three-Note Mystery
scenes.learningGoal: Compare possible explanations before calling a repeating pattern a discovery.

story.text: Beep. Beep-beep. The desk speaker goes quiet. Then the same three notes return. DUTİ rolls closer, holding a spoon as if it were a listening horn.
I tried asking it a question. It kept beeping. That is not a very useful answer.

On the screen, the pattern sits beside your old notes. It might come from nearby equipment. It might become clearer if you compare it with your measurements. A rover could look for its source without sending anyone outside.
We have a question, not an answer. Shall we study the pattern, follow the signal, or check the old equipment logs while we refill oxygen?

choices.label: Compare the three-note pattern
choices.futureConsequence: Keep a careful pattern record for the evidence comparison on Sol 9; an earlier rock study may make that comparison special.

feedback.text: I saved the pattern beside our measurements. Matching shapes can be a clue, but they do not explain themselves.

choices.label: Follow the signal with the rover
choices.futureConsequence: Locate an old survey relay without sending an astronaut outside. Earlier Earth guidance reduces this task to 1 Energy.

feedback.text: The rover found an old survey relay behind a ridge. A lantern symbol is painted on its case. This is equipment, not a visitor!

choices.label: Read the equipment logs and refill oxygen
choices.futureConsequence: Build the oxygen reserve and find the relay inventory entry, but miss today's new signal measurements.

feedback.text: The logs list a survey relay with a three-note test signal. We have a possible explanation and more oxygen. We have not measured where it is.

scenes.explorationPrompt: Let the child inspect a waveform, the rover camera, and a relay inventory page in any order. Finding a hotspot is optional and never an ending requirement.
scenes.hint: DUTİ places the new pattern beside the notebook from Sol 2. Some questions need more than one kind of record.

transition.note: Apply the usual shared transition using the extended mission forecast.

scenes.title: The Drawer Marked Tomorrow
scenes.learningGoal: Stored materials and records can carry earlier work forward, but preparation has opportunity costs.

story.text: A routine store-room check reveals a drawer labeled TOMORROW. DUTİ cannot resist reading the smaller print: For whoever asks the next good question.
Inside: an insulated plant tray, a spare recorder part, and a survey cassette. We can finish one careful job with our work time today.
If you kept plants growing, a living tray can be protected for the next crew. The recorder part could restore DUTİ's missing notebook pictures. The cassette could explain who left the relay outside.
Three ways to save something. Which kind of tomorrow should we prepare?

choices.label: Protect a living plant tray
choices.futureConsequence: Preserve plants already growing before arrival and their care notes. This can support a living-garden ending after the Sol 6 greenhouse study.

feedback.text: The living tray is protected, and its care instructions are ready. These are plants we kept growing, not seeds that grew overnight.

choices.unavailableReason: The greenhouse was shut down on Sol 3. No living experiment tray remains to protect.

choices.label: Restore DUTİ's notebook pictures
choices.futureConsequence: Recover DUTİ's saved pictures of earlier preparations. Spare supplies organized in 1B reduce this cost to 0 Energy.

feedback.text: My pictures are back! A packed shelter. A crew working together. I had saved the ordinary moments, too.

choices.label: Open the survey cassette
choices.futureConsequence: Recover a fictional older crew's relay-test log. Combine it with a located relay to investigate a network of instruments.

feedback.text: The cassette says the three notes are a test call from an old survey network. There may be more stations than the one in our equipment list.

scenes.explorationPrompt: Inspect the care label, recorder socket, and cassette diagram. If the greenhouse is off, show an empty, unlit tray instead of living plants.
scenes.hint: A tiny drawing on the cassette matches the lantern symbol in the equipment list.

transition.note: Apply the usual shared transition using the extended mission forecast.

scenes.title: Two Stories, One Signal
scenes.learningGoal: Separate observations from explanations, and label what remains uncertain.

story.text: A routine receiver check identifies the three-note call as an equipment test, even if you did not locate its source. Your notes cover the table. DUTİ lays two cards beside them: WHAT WE OBSERVED and WHAT WE STILL WONDER.
The three notes are from survey equipment. That part is no longer a mystery. But what should our next message help somebody discover?

You could compare the records to build an evidence report. You could record the crew's story alongside your measurements. Or you could use the work slot to maintain life support while a simple computer check finishes.
A good ending does not need every answer. It needs us to be honest about the answers we have.

choices.label: Compare the evidence and mark open questions
choices.futureConsequence: Connect the rock/pattern investigation or the relay/cassette investigation. Do not add a discovery that the actual history does not support.

feedback.text: Our report separates measurements from guesses. If two things look alike, we say they look alike; we do not claim that proves what caused them.

choices.label: Record the crew's story
choices.futureConsequence: Save voices and captions about the choices actually made. Restored DUTİ pictures can turn this into a special farewell.

feedback.text: We recorded what happened here, including the jobs that earned no Science Points. I put my smallest beep at the end.

choices.label: Maintain life support during the record check
choices.futureConsequence: Build oxygen reserves before the last sol. Keep existing records, but skip today's detailed comparison and crew recording.

feedback.text: Our oxygen reserve is stronger. The computer checked the files for readable data, but it did not do the deeper comparison or record our crew story.

scenes.explorationPrompt: Let the child move note cards into Observed and Still Wonder. The activity supports the chosen report and never changes costs or invents a missing record.
scenes.hint: DUTİ asks: Which two pages would somebody need to understand this clue?

transition.note: Apply the usual shared transition using the extended mission forecast.

scenes.title: A Light for Who Comes Next
scenes.learningGoal: Communicate discoveries and uncertainty, and recognize that a mission can leave different kinds of useful legacy.

story.text: The last planned sol arrives. Compass Outpost is quiet, but not empty: your notes are on the table, your work is in the rooms, and DUTİ has saved a place for the mission's final page.
Ten sols ago, we had a blank notebook. Look at it now.

One work slot remains. You can send a focused evidence packet to Earth, prepare a handover capsule for the next crew, or leave a welcome message in the outpost. What appears on the final page will depend on the trail you followed.
We do not have to leave every kind of treasure. We can leave the one we took the time to make.

choices.label: Send our evidence packet to Earth
choices.futureConsequence: Can reveal the rock-pattern or relay-network ending when the matching earlier investigation is complete. Acknowledge transmission locally; no instant Earth reply.

feedback.text: Packet sent. Earth will receive it after the signal travel time. Let us look at the story our choices made.

choices.label: Prepare the next crew's handover capsule
choices.futureConsequence: With the greenhouse study and a protected living tray, leave a garden handover. Otherwise leave only the actual records and materials collected.

feedback.text: The handover capsule is labeled with exactly what we saved. No imaginary harvests. No missing instructions. A real beginning for the next crew.

choices.label: Leave a welcome message in the outpost
choices.futureConsequence: A no-extra-cost final action. Restored pictures and a crew recording can reveal DUTİ's special memory-map farewell.

feedback.text: Welcome, next Commander. We left our questions where you can find them. DUTİ adds one final dot to the notebook.

scenes.explorationPrompt: Before the decision, show only items this mission actually created. After the decision, present one ending, its evidence, and one gentle replay invitation.
scenes.hint: The screen shows the notebook, transmission desk, and handover shelf. No ending names or combination checklist appears before the decision.

specialEndings.title: The Stone That Kept Time

story.text: Your close-up rock images fill the screen. Beside them sit the measurements you carefully compared. The repeating signal did not come from the stone: it came from equipment. But following the pattern made you look at the stone in a new way.
These stripes may record different chapters in how the rock formed. We have a question worth testing, and a sample ready for another scientist to study.
You label the packet: A question kept safe inside a stone. DUTİ adds a little clock beside the sample box. The screen shows SENT, not ANSWER RECEIVED.

evidence: You saved a physical sample on Sol 2.
You studied it in the laboratory on Sol 6.
You compared patterns and evidence before sending your report.
specialEndings.replayHint: A small thing saved early can become a much bigger question later.
specialEndings.scienceBoundary: Fictional research lead only. No confirmed rock age, water history, living organism, or NASA discovery is asserted.

specialEndings.title: The Smallest Garden on Mars

story.text: Inside the handover case, a protected tray holds plants your team kept alive. Beside it are the greenhouse measurements, care instructions, and a blank page labeled NEXT OBSERVATION.
We did not grow a whole farm. We kept one careful experiment going. Somebody else can ask the next question.
DUTİ slips the once-empty seed box onto the shelf beside the tray. Its label now reads: A garden is also a promise to look after something. The next page belongs to another crew.

evidence: You kept a full or smaller greenhouse operating.
You completed its study on Sol 6.
You protected a living tray and prepared its handover.
specialEndings.replayHint: Some discoveries need care long before the final day.
specialEndings.scienceBoundary: The tray was already growing before arrival. It is not a new ten-sol seed-to-harvest claim, a food-independent colony, or an oxygen supply.

specialEndings.title: DUTİ's Secret Constellation

story.text: DUTİ dims its screen. Small dots appear: the shelter you prepared, the room where the crew waited safely, and the desk where you restored its pictures. Thin lines join them into the outline of a little bear.
It is not a real constellation. It is my map of when we looked after one another. I was saving it for the last page.
Your crew recording begins. Behind the voices is DUTİ's smallest beep. You leave the map beside the welcome message, where the next Commander will find it.
We measured a lot of things. Thank you for remembering the people doing the measuring.

evidence: You prepared the shelter and used it during the alert.
You recorded the crew and left a welcome message.
specialEndings.replayHint: Not every important moment earns a Science Point.
specialEndings.scienceBoundary: A fictional memory-map image, not a real astronomical constellation or a claim that DUTİ is a living being.

specialEndings.title: The Lantern Network

story.text: The rover location and survey cassette finally fit together. One lantern symbol becomes several on the old map. Your careful comparison identifies the three-note call as a test message used by a fictional survey network.
Our panel work helped the power budget. Earth helped us use the robot efficiently. Then we kept the crew inside and let our machines investigate. Those choices brought these pieces together.
Your packet contains the relay location, the cassette log, and the questions still untested. Farther along the old map are other marked stations. No one claims they are working yet.
One signal answered. A whole map of questions left to ask.

evidence: You serviced the panels and received Earth's guidance.
You used the robot during the alert and later located the relay.
You opened the cassette, compared the evidence, and sent the packet.
specialEndings.replayHint: A useful reply, a careful preparation, and a machine doing the risky work can belong to the same story.
specialEndings.scienceBoundary: The older crew, survey network, cassette, and relay are fictional story props, not real NASA assets or an operational Mars network.

success.title: A Notebook Full of Questions
success.text: Ten sols complete. You protected the crew and reached the research target. Your notebook holds the discoveries you actually made, and open questions for the next crew. DUTİ closes the cover, then leaves a pencil tucked inside.
success.replayHint: Would a different trail of choices leave a different last page?

partial.title: One More Question
partial.text: You reached the last page, but part of the research or safety goal remains unfinished. Your completed work still matters. DUTİ marks one place to prepare differently next time. Show the actual Science and Safety shortfall.
partial.replayHint: Which earlier preparation might give your next mission more room to explore?

stopped.title: A Safe Pause
stopped.text: DUTİ helps the team stop work and begin the base's emergency procedures. Our research mission is paused. Show the resource or unavailable-choice reason, without a death scene or a claim that the depleted resource has refilled.
stopped.replayHint: We can try another plan. Which reserve needed help earlier?

endingResolution: Stop immediately if a resource is 0 or no option is available; no special ending.
After the Sol 10 decision and feedback only, evaluate successRequirements with no additional transition.
If requirements fail, use the partial ending and no special ending.

For a successful completed mission, select the matching special ending with the lowest priority number. Conditions require every allChoices entry and at least one choice in each anyChoiceGroups entry.
If none matches, use the ordinary success ending. Exactly one main ending is shown.
